## Metadata
Title: FUN's Cross-Word Puzzle
Author: Aloysius E. Pracny
Copyright: New York World
Date: 1914-07-26
Number: 29
Description: Five puzzles in one, laid out in one grid as printed with _ between the pieces: a zigzag band four squares wide down the left (17 rows, Nos. 1-36, 101-102), its mirror down the right (Nos. 37-72, 103-104), a 3x3 square at the top centre (73-80), a 4x4 square in the middle (81-92) and a 3x3 square at the bottom centre (93-100). On the page the two 3x3 squares sit half a square left of the 4x4's columns and the 4x4 half a square above the rows given here (r8-r11); they are placed at c10-c12 and r8-r11 as the nearest whole squares. No heading, title or number is printed with the puzzle (No. 29 is its place in the series); squares 71 and 72 (r1c18, r1c19) carry no printed number though the list uses them.
Source: Milwaukee Sentinel, 1914-07-26, p. 81
Solution-Source: Milwaukee Sentinel, 1914-08-02, p. 68


## Printed
intro: Here are five puzzles in one, a contribution for FUN'S puzzle solvers to ponder over, from Aloysius E. Pracny of Jackson street, Brooklyn. He writes as follows: "The pleasure I have found in solving the cross word puzzles in FUN has prompted me to construct the enclosed." Fill in the small squares with words corresponding to the list of clews and definitions given below, allowing one letter to each square. Then compare your solution with the one to be given in next week's FUN.
